title: Worksheet — Laws of Motion (Class 12 NIOS Physics)
instructions: Attempt all 10 questions. Show every step in subjective questions; choose one option for MCQs. Take g = 10 m/s² unless otherwise stated. Total time: 50 minutes.

questions.question: Action and reaction forces act on the same body.
questions.explanation: They act on different bodies — that's why they don't cancel.

questions.question: Linear momentum is defined as p = ____.
A 4-kg body is acted on by a 16-N net force. Its acceleration is:
A 5-kg block on a horizontal surface (μ_k = 0.2) is pushed by a 20-N horizontal force. Its acceleration is:
A 0.1-kg ball moving at 20 m/s is caught by a fielder, coming to rest in 0.05 s. Find (i) the impulse and (ii) the average force on the ball.
questions.answer: Δp = m(v_f − v_i) = 0.1(0 − 20) = −2 kg·m/s. So |Impulse| = 2 N·s, opposite to motion. Average force F = Δp/Δt = −2/0.05 = −40 N. Magnitude 40 N opposing motion.

questions.question: A 2-kg gun fires a 0.005-kg bullet horizontally at 500 m/s. Find the recoil velocity of the gun.
questions.answer: Momentum conservation (initial = 0): 0 = (2)(v_g) + (0.005)(500). So 2 v_g = −2.5 → v_g = −1.25 m/s. The gun recoils at 1.25 m/s opposite to the bullet's direction.

questions.question: Two blocks of masses 6 kg and 4 kg hang on either side of a frictionless pulley over an inextensible rope. Find the acceleration of the system and the tension.

A 5-kg block on an inclined plane at 30° with μ_k = 0.2 (g = 10 m/s²). (a) Draw the FBD and write equations along and perpendicular to the incline. (b) Find the acceleration of the block down the slope.
questions.answer: (a) Forces: weight mg = 50 N (vertical down); normal N (perpendicular to incline); friction f_k (up the slope, since the block slides down). Components: along the incline (down-slope = +): mg sin θ − f_k = m a → 25 − f_k = 5 a. Perpendicular: N − mg cos θ = 0 → N = mg cos θ = 50 × cos 30° = 50 × (√3/2) ≈ 43.30 N. (b) Kinetic friction f_k = μ_k N = 0.2 × 43.30 ≈ 8.66 N. So 25 − 8.66 = 5 a → a = 16.34/5 ≈ 3.27 m/s² down the slope. Equivalently a = g(sin θ − μ_k cos θ) = 10 × (0.5 − 0.2 × 0.866) = 10 × 0.327 = 3.27 m/s².

questions.question: (a) State Newton's three laws of motion. (b) Use Newton's third law to derive the conservation of linear momentum for two interacting particles in an isolated system. (c) A 3-kg ball moving at 8 m/s collides head-on with a stationary 1-kg ball; they stick together after collision. Find the common velocity afterwards.
questions.answer: (a) 1st: A body continues in rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless acted on by a net external force. 2nd: F = dp/dt; for constant mass F = ma. 3rd: To every action there is an equal-and-opposite reaction (acting on a different body). (b) Take two particles of masses m₁ and m₂ interacting only with each other. By Newton's 3rd law, F_(12) = −F_(21). Total momentum P = p₁ + p₂; differentiate: dP/dt = F_(net on 1) + F_(net on 2) = F_(12) + F_(21) = 0. So P = constant (conservation of linear momentum). (c) Momentum: 3 × 8 + 1 × 0 = (3 + 1) v → 24 = 4 v → v = 6 m/s in the same direction as the original motion.
questions.explanation: Standard derivation followed by an inelastic collision computation.
